notes.decision: Translated 'Some' as indefinite plural subject of ⲥⲉⲧⲏⲕ (3pl). Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲉ functions like ⲟⲩⲟⲛ 'some, certain ones' before a 3pl verb. The opponents are unspecified persecutors — the parallel structure of the page (Second Living Man : Apostle :: First Man : cosmogonic First Man) makes them rival groups within or against the Church.

'The Second Living Man' — apostolic figure (probably Mani or his apostolic predecessor), parallel to the cosmogonic First Man (ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ) of line 4. The typological structure: just as the First Man humbled the Darkness in primordial cosmogony, the Second (apostolic) Man is persecuted in the Church.
Read as Lyc ϯⲃⲓⲟ 'humbled, abased.' Causative-perfective: 'the First Man humbled the Darkness' — the cosmogonic victory expressed as humiliation/abasement of the dark powers.

ⲅⲣⲟ = 'prevail, conquer.' The clause is the chapter's thesis: the Darkness was conquered through the agency of the Five Greatnesses. Subject is implicit (the powers of light); ⲁⲣⲁⲩ 'over them' = over the dark powers.

Lycopolitan ⲩⲧⲟⲉ = ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'four.' With the perfective ⲁ-, the clause means '(then) the four (remaining) Greatnesses were revealed' — narratively bridging from the unitary first Greatness (Father in silence) to the four manifest emanations enumerated in lines 19-31. The article ⲡ- before ⲩⲧⲟⲉ may be elided/absorbed; transcription shows 'ⲁ ⲩⲧⲟⲉ' with space.

'The Mother of Life, the Great Spirit' — both standard Manichaean titles applied here apparently to the same figure as the Second Greatness, paired with ⲁⲍⲁⲛ ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'beside the First Man.' The 'Great Spirit' apposition with the Mother is unusual in canonical schemata (where Living Spirit is masculine and a separate emanation), and the schema here groups the Mother+First Man+Five Sons together as the Second Greatness.

'The Great Builder' — ⲉⲕⲱⲧ = ⲕⲱⲧ 'builder, fashioner.' This is the Manichaean Great Architect (μέγας Δημιουργός), here grouped under the Third Greatness alongside the Beloved of the Lights and the Living Spirit with his Five Sons.

Note the ordinal mismatch with canonical Manichaean catalogues: here the Third Ambassador is the Fourth Greatness in the page's own counting. The 'Third' in his title is preserved as a fixed epithet (per accumulated vocabulary), even when the local enumeration places him in fourth position.
'Jesus the Radiance' — fixed translation per terminology guide. The Fifth Greatness, identified directly with Jesus and his powers/emanations.

'The whole Building' — the cosmic construction (the entire fashioned cosmos). The Five Sons of the First Man are connected with the whole Building, while the Five Sons of the Living Spirit are spread out as bearers in five places — referencing the Manichaean cosmological architecture where the Living Spirit's sons are the cosmic supports/bearers (Splenditenens, King of Glory, etc.).
